answer: Proof of Stake protocols resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral, effectively turning identity verification into a fiscal burden. If an attacker fragments their influence to reach a nadir of network integrity, they must exhaust substantial resources to purchase enough stake. Like the shale beneath a surface, the underlying value prevents cheap identity replication. A whispering validator node cannot whisper fraudulent state transitions without risking the forfeiture of this locked stake, forcing adversaries to bear the full cost of subversion.
